questions.q: Which amine does NOT give a foul-smelling product when heated with CHCl₃ and alcoholic KOH?
questions.explain: Forming R–N≡C requires the nitrogen to lose two hydrogens; N-methylaniline is a secondary amine with only one N–H. The test works for both aliphatic and aromatic primary amines, including tert-butylamine.

questions.q: The reactive intermediate in the carbylamine reaction is:
questions.explain: OH⁻ removes the H of CHCl₃ and CCl₃⁻ loses Cl⁻ (α-elimination) to give :CCl₂, which is attacked by the amine nitrogen. The same carbene is the electrophile in the Reimer–Tiemann reaction.

questions.q: Aniline is heated with chloroform and ethanolic KOH. The organic product is:
questions.explain: The product is an isocyanide, bonded through nitrogen, not the nitrile. Nitriles come from alkyl halides with KCN; isocyanides come from the carbylamine reaction or from alkyl halides with AgCN.

questions.q: In the balanced equation for the carbylamine reaction, RNH₂ + CHCl₃ + x KOH → RNC + x KCl + x H₂O, the value of x is:
questions.explain: All three Cl atoms of chloroform leave: one as Cl⁻ in forming :CCl₂, and two as HCl removed from R–NH–CHCl₂, so three KOH, three KCl and three H₂O appear.
